paper.title: Algorithm 790: CSHEP2D: Cubic Shepard method for bivariate interpolation of scattered data
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 25(1), 70-73 (TOMS 790, March 1999)

code.archive: sha256 ac71fab09b7dd3715c0b1bb79bc77d3d95bcfd46141935a2cd9e2df1837718ff (netlib.org/toms/790.gz as fetched 2026-11-26, HTTP 200, 3273 lines once decompressed)
code.note: Fortran 77 shar archive. Remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line and run it with sh to create Fortran77/Drivers/Sp/ (driver1.f, driver2.f, data1, res1, res1_2, res2), and Fortran77/Src/ with the CSHEP2D sources (src.f: CSHEP2, CS2VAL, CS2GRD, CS2HES, GETNP2, STORE2 etc.; src_792.f: TESTDT, TSTFN1, TSTFN2 test-set routines). driver1.f is interactive: it reads node set, function range, NC, NW and NR from standard input, and writes its report to the file res1_2 (OPEN(LOUT,FILE='res1_2')). Compare the first data row of the report with the claim below.

claim.location: The shipped reference output res1_2 (member of 790.gz), report header 'Node set 1 N = 100 NI = 33 NC = 17 NW = 30 NR = 6', first data row 'Function 1 Max Error 0.0451'.

reference.file: Drivers/Sp/res1_2 (member of 790.gz), node set 1, function 1, Max Error column

claim.metric: Max Error for interpolation function 1 (CS2TST, node set 1, N=100, NI=33 uniform grid, NC=17, NW=30, NR=6), as printed by driver1 to res1_2, compared with 0.0451 from the shipped reference.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled and was not read.

values.name: CS2TST node set 1, function 1, Max Error (4 decimal print)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference prints Max Error with four decimals, so 5e-5 absolute is half of the last printed unit: a double-precision rerun of the same algorithm must land in the same printed bin. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one Fortran compile and a run over 100 nodes on a 33 by 33 grid.
cost.data_size: None beyond the archive (data is generated by TESTDT).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: CSHEP2D is a scattered-data interpolation code whose archive ships a reference report of interpolation errors on a generated node set, so the claim is a checkable number the code must compute.
